children: A federal judge ordered President Trump to temporarily restore White House access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists, days after the news organizations were banned over their coverage of the administration.
The removal of reporters' press badges was likely done without "constitutionally adequate due process," federal judge Timothy Kelly said in a ruling issued early Thursday.
"The 'general rule' is that 'individuals must receive notice and an opportunity to be heard before the Government deprives them' of a constitutionally protected interest," Kelly wrote.

CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a lawsuit Monday after journalists from the outlets were banned from the White House over the weekend. They said they had done so to "protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes."

The suit, filed in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., had been assigned to Kelly, a Trump appointee. The news organizations were seeking a temporary restraining order that would force the administration to reinstate their reporters' hard passes while the litigation proceeds.

Representatives for CNN, MS NOW, and Politico said their journalists were turned away from White House grounds early Saturday. The following day, CNN reporters were removed from a scheduled pool coverage assignment at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

The suit marks an escalation of tensions between the press and the Trump administration after the president who has often sought to target news organizations throughout his second term, suing several outlets-including The Wall Street Journal-for defamation, barring Associated Press journalists from the Oval Office, and issuing subpoenas to reporters.

The administration has also curtailed access at the Pentagon, which last year imposed strict rules limiting news gathering-prompting several major outlets to surrender their credentials rather than comply.
First Amendment attorneys and media executives have said the administration's actions represent a coordinated effort to intimidate news outlets and discourage confidential sources from speaking out.
